主要内容: Nike reported its fiscal fourth-quarter 2019 earnings, which slightly missed analysts' expectations. Revenues increased by 4% to just over $10 billion, driven by higher sales of sneakers and sports gear. However, the company's earnings per share of 62 cents fell short of the forecasted 66 cents. Nike's margins were impacted by its direct-to-consumer investments. The brand's revenue, excluding Converse, rose 10% to $9.7 billion, while Converse sales remained flat at $491 million. North America sales increased 8% to $4.17 billion, and China sales surged 22% to $1.70 billion. Nike has faced challenges in growing sales in the U.S. due to competition from brands like Adidas and Lululemon. Footwear sales in North America rose 9%, while apparel and equipment sales grew by 6% and 7%, respectively. Nike's direct-to-consumer division generated $11.8 billion in revenue, fueled by a 35% increase in online sales. The company also emphasized its efforts to expand its women's business and improve customer engagement through initiatives like the Nike Fit app. Nike reported its fiscal fourth-quarter 2019 earnings, highlighting its continued focus on expanding its women's business and leveraging digital opportunities. The company noted that its direct-to-consumer women's business is still outperforming the wholesale channel. Despite ongoing trade tensions between the U.S. and China, Nike emphasized its strong presence in the Chinese market, stating that consumer sentiment remains positive. Nike's stock closed up over 1% on Thursday, with a year-to-date increase of 17%, contributing to a market cap of approximately $131.4 billion. The stock has significantly outperformed the S&P 500 Retail ETF (XRT), which has declined by 14% over the same period.
